statement.p: Evaluate the triple integral of f(x,y,z)=z(x^2+y^2+z^2)^{-3/2} over the part of the ball x^2+y^2+z^2\le 36 defined by z\ge 3.

static.solution:
The equation of the sphere in spherical coordinates is {\rho }^2=36 or \rho =6.
\rho_0=6
We write the equation of the plane z=3 in spherical coordinates: \rho \cos \phi =3\quad\Rightarrow\quad \rho =\frac{3}{ \cos \phi } To compute the interval of \phi, we must find the value of \phi corresponding to \rho =6 on the plane z=3. We get 6= \frac{3}{ \cos \phi }\quad\Rightarrow\quad \cos \phi =\frac{1}{2}\quad\Rightarrow\quad \phi =\frac{\pi }{3} Therefore, \phi is changing from 0 to \frac{\pi }{3}, \theta is changing from 0 to 2\pi, and \rho is changing from \frac{3}{ \cos \phi } to 6.
We obtain the following description for \mathcal{W}: \mathcal{W}: \,0\le \theta \le 2\pi,\, 0\le \phi \le \frac{\pi }{3},\, \frac{3}{ \cos \phi }\le \rho \le 6 The function is f( x,y,z )=z{({x}^2+{y}^2+{z}^2)}^{-3/2}=\rho \cos \phi \cdot {({\rho }^2)}^{-3/2}={\rho }^{-2} \cos \phi We use triple integrals in spherical coordinates to write \begin{array}{rcl} \int\!\!\int\!\!\int _{\mathcal{W}} f( x,y,z ) \,dV \amp =\amp \int_0^{2\pi } \int_0^{\pi/3} \int_{3/\cos\phi}^{6} ({\rho }^{-2} \cos \phi ){\rho }^2 \sin \phi\, d\rho \, d\phi \,d\theta\\ \quad \amp =\amp \int_0^{2\pi } \int_0^{\pi/3} \int_{3/\cos\phi}^{6} \frac{ \sin 2\phi }{2} \,d\rho \, d\phi \,d\theta\\ \quad \amp =\amp \int_0^{2\pi } \int_0^{\pi/3} \frac{ \sin 2\phi }{2} \rho \bigg|_{\rho=\frac{3}{ \cos \phi }}^{6} d\phi \,d\theta\\ \quad \amp =\amp \int_0^{2\pi } \int_0^{\pi/3} \left(3 \sin 2\phi -\frac{ \sin 2\phi }{2}\cdot \frac{3}{ \cos \phi }\right) d\phi \,d\theta\\ \quad \amp =\amp \int_0^{2\pi } \int_0^{\pi/3} ( 3 \sin 2\phi -3 \sin \phi ) \,d\phi \,d\theta\\ \quad \amp =\amp 2\pi \cdot 3 \cdot\left(-\frac{\cos 2\phi}{2} + \cos \phi \bigg|_{\phi =0}^{\pi/3}\right)\\ \quad \amp =\amp \pi \cdot 6\cdot\left(-\frac{\cos \frac{2\pi }{3}}{2}+ \cos \frac{\pi }{3}+\frac12-1\right)\\ \quad \amp =\amp 1.5\pi \end{array}
